mt_psychology_wall.blurb: A bolted face on the west side of Kalispell, and the first wall you meet at Kila Crags. It holds ten sport routes, running from the high 5.7s through the 5.10s with one 5.11. Most of the climbing is moderate, so it suits climbers working through 5.9 and 5.10. The face is clean and gives pleasant, steady climbing, but loose rock has been flagged here, so wear a helmet and test holds. Anchors at the top make lowering straightforward, and the crag is easy to top-rope from a trail on the east side. Expect local company on weekends.

mt_confluence_crag.blurb: A newer southeast-facing cliff above the camp where the Lake Fork joins the main stem of Rock Creek, south of Red Lodge. Ten bolted lines cover the 5.10 to low 5.12 range, with five in the 5.10s and most of the rest at 5.11. The wall is steeper than it looks from below and tends to give a quick, strong pump. It catches sun through the middle of the day, with shade coming on later in the afternoon. Because the cliff is still young, some loose rock remains despite cleaning, so a helmet is wise. All anchors are double bolts with chains.

mt_ovens_the.blurb: A small, popular limestone sport wall a few miles above Red Lodge, in the foothills near the ski area. Ten routes sit on tilted fins right beside the road, ranging from an easy 5.5 up to the 5.10s, with most between 5.7 and 5.10. Climbs are around 65 feet, so a longer rope than a 40 meter is useful. The rock is fairly soft but well bolted, and the grayer stone is the more solid. The very short walk and beginner-friendly grades make it a good warm-up spot. The wall gets sun earlier in the day and shades over later in the afternoon.
